ceiling_directive: Extend the all-count Bayes bridge from the single contrast c-dagger to the one-versus-many family c=(1,-w), proving uniform local, exterior, and proper-face bounds and a matching unrestricted second-order coefficient.
improvement_directive: Parameterize the face-robust tube and directional ledger by arbitrary positive one-versus-many weights, then prove the design-independent converse uniformly over every allocation count so that the fixed-q-star expansion becomes an unrestricted minimax expansion for that family.
critique: The unrestricted sharp limit is proved only for the hand-picked contrast c-dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4), whereas the motivating problem asks for L(c) and the equality-or-loss decision for general permitted contrasts; outside c-dagger, the note proves only the fixed-independent benchmark. That contrast-specific result is too narrow to establish a general multiarm second-order framework, and the paper supplies neither a nontrivial contrast family nor practical numerical certificates demonstrating the value of the exact coefficient. The general fixed-independent theorem also relies on lem:unit-airy-feedback-bounds, which is stated without proof or a precise external citation, so that advertised general component is not fully discharged as written. The later unequal-three-arm-qstar-liminf-corollary says that no unrestricted equality is asserted and calls its one-sided statement the strongest surviving result, directly contradicting the proved sharp-limit theorem for the same c-dagger and leaving stale claim-fidelity prose in the manuscript. These scope, proof-completeness, and coherence problems constrain the projected leading-journal score despite the contrast-specific converse and achievability claims. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
